newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees palm oil output rising in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees palm oil output rising in 1997.

text.p: The chairman of Indonesia's commodities regulator BULOG, Beddu Amang, said on Tuesday the country's crude palm oil production was projected to rise to 5.2-5.3 million tonnes in 1997, compared with 4.5 million tonnes last year.
"Last year's production was 4.5 million tonnes. Production this year will be around 5.2-5.3 million tonnes," Amang told reporters after meeting President Suharto.
He said the price of palm olein had increased to 1,640 rupiah/kg from 1,380 rupiah in July. Amang added that the "appropriate" price was 1,600 rupiah/kg.
"The increase was due to a reduction in supply to the local market because of increased exports," Amang said.
He said exports have been increasing following a reduction in the export taxes on crude palm oil and its products under the government's economic deregulation package in July.
Amang also said state plantations would increase their monthly crude palm oil allocations to BULOG to 20,000 tonnes from 10,000 tonnes previously.
"The deregulation package encourages exports. Our duty to stabilise local prices has been made difficult, therefore we have asked state plantations for additional supply," he said.

BULOG intervenes in the palm oil market when it considers prices are not reasonable. Local palm olein prices stood at 1,650-60 rupiah/kg on Tuesday, compared with 1,570 rupiah last Friday. Prices have been increasing in adjustment to the rupiah's weakening against the U.S. dollar and export values.
